test_title: PYST 60: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 23 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: What is the function of plasma in human blood?

options.text: It carries oxygen from lungs to all parts of the body.
It maintains the oxygen-rich blood supply to tissues.
It transports food, carbon dioxide and waste materials.
It helps in clotting blood during injuries.

solution:
The correct answer is __**It transports food, carbon dioxide and waste materials.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Blood Plasma** is a pale yellow liquid component of blood that holds the blood cells in whole blood in suspension. It makes up about **55%** of the body's total blood volume.
 
• The primary function of **plasma** is to **transport nutrients** (food), **hormones**, and **proteins** to the parts of the body that need them. It also carries **waste products** like **urea** and **carbon dioxide** from the cells to the excretory organs. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• **Red Blood Cells (RBCs)**, or erythrocytes, contain a protein called **hemoglobin**, which binds to **oxygen**. The primary role of carrying **oxygen** from the **lungs** to all body parts is performed by **RBCs**, not the plasma itself. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• Maintaining an **oxygen-rich blood supply** to tissues is the physiological responsibility of the **circulatory system** driven by the **heart** and mediated by **hemoglobin** in **red blood cells**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• While plasma contains **clotting factors** (like **fibrinogen**), the primary cellular component that helps in **clotting blood** during injuries to prevent excessive bleeding is the **platelets** (thrombocytes). ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Composition of Plasma:**
 
 
• **Water**: Approximately **90-92%** of plasma is water, which acts as a **solvent** for transporting various substances.
 
• **Plasma Proteins**: These include **Albumin** (maintains osmotic pressure), **Globulins** (involved in **immunity**/antibodies), and **Fibrinogen** (essential for **blood coagulation**).
 
• **Electrolytes**: Ions like **Sodium (Na+)**, **Chloride (Cl-)**, and **Bicarbonate (HCO3-)** help maintain **pH balance** and osmotic pressure.
 
 
 
• **Functions in Homeostasis:**
 
 
• **Plasma** plays a critical role in maintaining a constant **body temperature** by absorbing and distributing heat throughout the body.
 
• It helps in maintaining the **acid-base balance (pH)** of the body, which is vital for various **biochemical reactions**.
 
 
 
• **Transport Mechanism:**
 
 
• **Carbon dioxide** is transported in the plasma mainly in the form of **bicarbonate ions** (about **70%**), while a small amount is dissolved directly in the plasma.
 
• **Nutrients** absorbed from the **digestive tract**, such as **glucose**, **amino acids**, and **lipids**, are dissolved in the plasma to be delivered to **tissues**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Serum vs. Plasma**: **Serum** is the liquid part of blood that remains after **blood clotting** has occurred. It is essentially **plasma** without the **clotting factors** (like **fibrinogen**).
 
• **Blood pH**: The **pH** of human blood is slightly **alkaline**, typically ranging between **7.35 and 7.45**. Plasma acts as a **buffer** to keep this range stable.
 
• **Discovery**: The technique for **plasma storage** and its use for transfusions was significantly advanced by **Dr. Charles Drew** in the **1940s**.
</ul
